events.label: Holmes begins to tell Watson the supposed murder case involving Colonel Barclay

communicates.speaker: character_holmes
communicates.content: Then, if you are not too sleepy, I will give you a sketch of what has happened, and of what remains to be done. It is the supposed murder of Colonel Barclay, of the Royal Mallows, at Aldershot, which I am investigating. The facts are only two days old. Briefly they are these:

events.label: Holmes describes Mrs. Barclay going to a Guild meeting and returning to Lachine
Mrs. Barclay goes into the morning-room at Lachine, lights a lamp, and rings for tea
Colonel Barclay joins Mrs. Barclay in the morning-room
Tea is brought and the maid hears voices in furious altercation; the door is locked from the inside
The servants agree only two voices are heard and the dispute includes repeated cries from Mrs. Barclay

communicates.speaker: character_crooked_man_woman
communicates.content: What can be done now? Give me back my life. I will never so much as breathe the same air with you again! You coward!

events.label: After screams, the coachman attempts to enter but then enters through an open side of the French window onto the lawn
Colonel Barclay is found dead in a pool of blood; Mrs. Barclay is insensible on a couch
The coachman cannot find the key; he seeks a policeman and a medical man and returns
Mrs. Barclay is removed to her room while the Colonel’s body is placed on the sofa and the scene is examined
Police examine a jagged cut on the Colonel’s head caused by a violent blow and find a hard carved wooden club with a bone handle near the body
Search finds no missing key on Mrs. Barclay, the victim, or anywhere in the room; the door is eventually opened by a locksmith from Aldershot
Holmes goes down to Aldershot on Tuesday morning at Major Murphy’s request

clues.significance: Police found a hard carved wooden club with a bone handle lying close to Colonel Barclay’s body during their careful examination of the scene of the quarrel.
Police reported that the missing key was not found on Mrs. Barclay, on the victim, or anywhere in the room during their search.
Holmes obtained five clear impressions of a man’s footmarks, including one in the roadway, two on the lawn, and two faint ones on stained boards near the window.
Holmes inferred the creature had five well-marked footpads and long nails from tracings of footmarks on the tissue paper.
Holmes inferred the creature could run up a curtain based on traces showing it ran up the curtain.
